card.name: Dose-adjustment wording in interaction text
card.fires_on: The word dose or dosage, or a small word just before one, in sentences about changing a drug amount (reduce, adjust, increase). Also a few spots in general text where a word is about to be followed by a noun like pattern or position.

modes.label: Dose or dosage before reduction/adjustment
modes.description: The word dose or dosage (or its first letter piece) where a change in amount is being described.
modes.example: A<< dose>> reduction of PROGRAF should be considered

modes.label: Linking word before dose terms
modes.description: A small word such as be, with, and, or over just before a dose or estimation term.
modes.example: The dosage of the anticoagulants should<< be>> reduced to maintain the PT/INR

modes.label: Non-drug text on patterns
modes.description: Words in linguistics or music text where a grouping or position term follows.

card.writes: It seems to nudge output away from words like scheduling, routing and positioning.
card.plain: It lights up on wording about changing a drug dose, especially in interaction warnings.
